Read an XBRL taxonomy package

Source: R/taxonomy.R
read_taxonomy.Rd

Opens a taxonomy package – a ZIP, or a directory already unpacked from one – and returns the object add_taxonomy() needs to give a filing's facts their names, their place in a statement, and their sign convention.

Usage

read_taxonomy(path, exdir = NULL)

Arguments

path

Path to a taxonomy package .zip, or to a directory holding an unpacked one.

exdir

Directory to unpack a ZIP into. Defaults to a session temporary directory; give a stable path to unpack each package only once. On Windows keep it short: the deepest names inside a Danish package are long enough that a long exdir pushes the total past the 260-character path limit.

Value

An object of class cvrr_taxonomy: a list with version, path, entrypoints (the entry point schemas it offers), defaults (the member that applies when a dimension is absent) and the internals add_taxonomy() uses.

Why this is a separate step

An XBRL instance carries facts, contexts and units and no readable text at all. Every label, every statement hierarchy, every debit/credit marking lives in the taxonomy the filing names in one link:schemaRef. That URI is an identifier, not a download address – for Danish filings the host it points at answers 404 – so the package has to be obtained separately and resolved locally. META-INF/catalog.xml holds the rewrite rules that map the URI onto a path inside the archive, and this function follows them.

Get the Danish packages from Erhvervsstyrelsen's Taksonomier, aktuelle and Taksonomier, historiske pages. One package per year is needed: the version a filing declares follows when it was prepared, not its accounting year, so a single year of accounts routinely spans several.

An archive without a catalog

Some archives in circulation are repacks and carry no META-INF/catalog.xml – the 20171001 taxonomy is only obtainable that way, and 31 filings of a 4,304-filing corpus declare it.

All the catalog does for these packages is map http://archprod.service.eogs.dk/taxonomy/<version>/ onto the directory the files sit in, and the archive states the version in its own layout. Where there is no catalog that mapping is reconstructed from the entry point schemas' location, and a warning says so: it is a convention read off the archive, not a rule the archive declared.

See also

add_taxonomy() to join a filing's facts to it, read_xbrl() to read the filing.

Other taxonomy: add_taxonomy(), check_breakdown(), check_cascade(), check_cashflow(), check_continuity(), check_inclusion(), check_movement(), check_statement(), xbrl_accounts(), xbrl_company(), xbrl_fill(), xbrl_lines(), xbrl_movements(), xbrl_note_tables(), xbrl_panel(), xbrl_period(), xbrl_ratios(), xbrl_report(), xbrl_report_data(), xbrl_resolve(), xbrl_robustness(), xbrl_screen(), xbrl_standardise(), xbrl_validate()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
tax <- read_taxonomy("XBRL20241001.zip")
tax$entrypoints
tax$defaults
} # }
